## Purpose and experimental design

Peak biomass was measured after management treatments were implemented in a
split-plot randomized complete block design (four blocks per location). Clover
species was assigned to whole plots and management to subplots.

The **core trial** includes Tillage, Strip-till, and V4 inter-row mowing at
Musgrave and Farm Hub. The **Musgrave mowing trial** compares four strip-till
management treatments, excluding Tillage. Biweekly autonomous mowing began at
V4 and continued every two weeks through VT. These analyses share observations
and are not independent experiments. Spring biomass is **not included**.
Legume biomass was measured during peak weed sampling, not necessarily at peak
legume growth.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(lmerTest)
library(glmmTMB)
library(emmeans)
library(DHARMa)

figure_dir <- here("figures", "peak_biomass")
table_dir <- here("output", "tables", "peak_biomass")
dir.create(figure_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(table_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 16))

species_colors <- c("Mammoth red clover" = "#C77C7D",
                    "Yellow sweetclover" = "#E9E6BD")
core_levels <- c("Tillage", "Strip-till", "V4 inter-row mowing")
mowing_levels <- c("Strip-till", "V4 inter-row mowing",
                   "V4 autonomous mowing", "Biweekly autonomous mowing")
all_levels <- c("Tillage", mowing_levels)
save_figure <- function(p, name, width = 11, height = 6) {
  ggsave(file.path(figure_dir, name), plot = p,
         width = width, height = height, units = "in", dpi = 300)
}
write_table <- function(x, name) {
  write.csv(as.data.frame(x), file.path(table_dir, name),
            row.names = FALSE, na = "")
}
```

## Import and validation

```{r import}
path <- here("data", "processed", "combined_processed.rds")
stopifnot(file.exists(path))
dat <- readRDS(path)
required <- c("location", "block_id", "whole_plot_id", "plot_id",
              "clover_species", "management", "peak_weed_biomass_kg_ha",
              "peak_legume_biomass_kg_ha",
              "peak_weed_biomass_g_0_5m2_below_detection")
if (length(setdiff(required, names(dat))))
  stop("Missing fields: ", paste(setdiff(required, names(dat)), collapse = ", "))
if (anyDuplicated(dat$plot_id)) stop("Duplicate subplot identifiers")
if (anyNA(dat[required])) stop("Missing design or outcome values")
for (response in c("peak_weed_biomass_kg_ha", "peak_legume_biomass_kg_ha")) {
  if (any(!is.finite(dat[[response]]) | dat[[response]] < 0))
    stop("Invalid biomass values: ", response)
}

dat <- dat |>
  mutate(location = factor(as.character(location),
                           levels = c("farmhub", "musgrave"),
                           labels = c("Farm Hub", "Musgrave")),
         clover_species = factor(as.character(clover_species),
                                 levels = names(species_colors)),
         management = factor(dplyr::recode(as.character(management),
                    "Between-row autonomous mowing" = "Biweekly autonomous mowing"),
                    levels = all_levels),
         block_id = factor(block_id),
         whole_plot_id = factor(whole_plot_id))
if (anyNA(dat[c("location", "clover_species", "management")]))
  stop("Unrecognized treatment or location level")

design <- dat |>
  group_by(location, block_id, clover_species, whole_plot_id) |>
  summarise(n_subplots = n(), .groups = "drop")
if (nrow(design) != 16 ||
    any(design$n_subplots != ifelse(design$location == "Musgrave", 5, 3)) ||
    any(design |> count(whole_plot_id) |> pull(n) != 1))
  stop("Unexpected split-plot structure")
core <- dat |>
  filter(management %in% core_levels) |>
  mutate(management = droplevels(management),
         block_id = droplevels(block_id),
         whole_plot_id = droplevels(whole_plot_id))
tool <- dat |>
  filter(location == "Musgrave", management %in% mowing_levels) |>
  mutate(location = droplevels(location),
         management = droplevels(management),
         block_id = droplevels(block_id),
         whole_plot_id = droplevels(whole_plot_id))
stopifnot(nrow(core) == 48, nrow(tool) == 32,
          n_distinct(core$whole_plot_id) == 16,
          n_distinct(tool$whole_plot_id) == 8)
knitr::kable(design, caption = "Whole-plot design and subplot counts")
write_table(design, "peak_biomass_design.csv")
```

## Descriptive treatment means

Within each location × species × management cell, four blocks supply four
subplot observations. Tables and figures show **raw means ± SE**, not
model-estimated means. Species effects are tested using the whole-plot
randomization in the models below.

```{r summaries}
summarize_biomass <- function(x) {
  x |>
    pivot_longer(c(peak_weed_biomass_kg_ha, peak_legume_biomass_kg_ha),
                 names_to = "response", values_to = "biomass_kg_ha") |>
    group_by(location, clover_species, management, response) |>
    summarise(n = n(), mean_kg_ha = mean(biomass_kg_ha),
              sd_kg_ha = sd(biomass_kg_ha),
              se_kg_ha = sd_kg_ha / sqrt(n),
              n_zero = sum(biomass_kg_ha == 0), .groups = "drop")
}
core_summary <- summarize_biomass(core)
tool_summary <- summarize_biomass(tool)
knitr::kable(core_summary, digits = 1, caption = "Core trial: observed biomass")
knitr::kable(tool_summary, digits = 1, caption = "Musgrave mowing trial: observed biomass")
write_table(core_summary, "core_peak_biomass_means.csv")
write_table(tool_summary, "musgrave_tool_peak_biomass_means.csv")
```

## Descriptive figures

Each figure has its own chunk and export. Only the specified response is
plotted; error bars represent mean ± raw SE for that response.

```{r figure-helper, include=FALSE}
biomass_figure <- function(x, response_name, plot_title, by_location = TRUE) {
  pdat <- x |> filter(.data$response == .env$response_name)
  if (!nrow(pdat) || any(as.character(pdat$response) != response_name))
    stop("Unexpected response in figure: ", response_name)
  p <- ggplot(pdat,
              aes(management, mean_kg_ha, fill = clover_species)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = .8), width = .7,
             color = "black", linewidth = .3) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = pmax(0, mean_kg_ha - se_kg_ha),
                      ymax = mean_kg_ha + se_kg_ha),
                  position = position_dodge(width = .8), width = .16) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = species_colors) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) gsub(" ", "\n", x, fixed = TRUE)) +
    labs(title = plot_title,
         x = NULL, y = expression("Biomass (kg ha"^{-1}*")"),
         fill = "Clover species",
         caption = "Observed treatment means ± raw SE (n = 4 blocks per cell).") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = .5, size = 11),
          legend.position = "bottom", plot.caption = element_text(size = 11))
  if (by_location) p <- p + facet_wrap(~location, scales = "free_y")
  p
}
```

## Mixed models

One initial model is fitted for each response × trial combination (four total).
Weed biomass is modeled with a log-Gaussian LMM.
Legume biomass has many exact zeros and is modeled with a Tweedie GLMM
(`1 < p < 2`, log link). These are **initial** models, subject to diagnostics.

The core weed analysis retains all 48 observations for descriptive statistics,
but excludes one below-detection-limit observation (Musgrave plot 310,
`<0.01 g`, represented as 0.1 kg ha^-1) for the preliminary log-Gaussian
inference model. The original 48-observation model is retained as a sensitivity
check; both models led to the same conclusions for the tested effects. The
three-way location × species × management interaction was also examined using
an ML likelihood-ratio test and was not supported (p = 0.487). The reduced
two-way-interaction model is retained.

Because legume biomass has near-complete
zeros in some combinations, its preliminary model is deliberately additive;
species × management interactions can be considered if supported later.
Random intercepts represent blocks and species whole plots nested within blocks.
The identifiers `block_id` and `whole_plot_id` are unique across locations;
therefore `(1 | block_id) + (1 | whole_plot_id)` specifies the intended nesting
without needing to repeat the block identifier in the whole-plot term.

```{r models}
core_weed_model <- lmerTest::lmer(
  log(peak_weed_biomass_kg_ha) ~
    location * clover_species + location * management +
    clover_species * management +
    (1 | block_id) + (1 | whole_plot_id), data = core)
core_weed_sensitivity_data <- core |>
  filter(!peak_weed_biomass_g_0_5m2_below_detection)
stopifnot(nrow(core_weed_sensitivity_data) == 47)
core_weed_reference <- update(core_weed_model,
                              data = core_weed_sensitivity_data)
tool_weed_model <- lmerTest::lmer(
  log(peak_weed_biomass_kg_ha) ~ clover_species * management +
    (1 | block_id) + (1 | whole_plot_id), data = tool)
core_legume_model <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
  peak_legume_biomass_kg_ha ~ location + clover_species + management +
    (1 | block_id) + (1 | whole_plot_id),
  family = glmmTMB::tweedie(link = "log"), data = core)
tool_legume_model <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
  peak_legume_biomass_kg_ha ~ clover_species + management +
    (1 | block_id) + (1 | whole_plot_id),
  family = glmmTMB::tweedie(link = "log"), data = tool)

```

## Core trial: weed biomass

### Diagnostics

The reference analysis uses 47 observations; the original 48-observation
model is retained above for sensitivity comparison. Model diagnostics refer
to the 47-observation reference fit.

```{r diagnostic-functions, include=FALSE}
model_ok <- function(m) {
  if (inherits(m, "glmmTMB")) {
    v <- tryCatch(vcov(m)$cond, error = function(e) NULL)
    return(isTRUE(m$sdr$pdHess) && isTRUE(m$fit$convergence == 0) &&
             !is.null(v) && all(is.finite(v)))
  }
  !lme4::isSingular(m) && !length(m@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages)
}
show_diagnostics <- function(m) {
  cat("Convergence/covariance checks passed:", model_ok(m), "\n")
  print(summary(m))
  print(VarCorr(m))
  set.seed(123)
  sim <- tryCatch(DHARMa::simulateResiduals(m, n = 1000),
                  error = function(e) {
                    cat("Simulation unavailable:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
                    NULL
                  })
  if (!is.null(sim)) {
    plot(sim)
    print(DHARMa::testUniformity(sim))
    print(DHARMa::testDispersion(sim))
    print(DHARMa::testOutliers(sim))
  }
}
```

```{r core-weed-diagnostics, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
show_diagnostics(core_weed_reference)
```

### ANOVA and within-location management comparisons

The location × management interaction is significant. Consequently,
management contrasts are evaluated **within location**, averaged across clover
species. Comparisons are unadjusted Fisher LSD-style (`adjust = "none"`) and
use Satterthwaite degrees of freedom. Contrasts are estimated on the log scale;
raw arithmetic treatment means ± SE are reported in the descriptive figures.

```{r core-weed-inference, results='asis'}
core_weed_anova <- as.data.frame(anova(core_weed_reference, type = 2,
                                       ddf = "Satterthwaite"))
core_weed_anova$term <- rownames(core_weed_anova)
rownames(core_weed_anova) <- NULL
core_weed_anova <- core_weed_anova[, c("term", setdiff(names(core_weed_anova), "term"))]
knitr::kable(core_weed_anova, digits = 4,
             caption = "Core weed biomass: Type II tests (47 observations)")
write_table(core_weed_anova, "core_weed_anova.csv")

core_weed_emm <- emmeans::emmeans(core_weed_reference,
                                  ~ management | location,
                                  lmer.df = "satterthwaite")
core_weed_contrasts <- as.data.frame(summary(
  pairs(core_weed_emm, adjust = "none"),
  infer = c(TRUE, TRUE), adjust = "none"))
knitr::kable(core_weed_contrasts, digits = 3,
             caption = "Core weed biomass: unadjusted management comparisons within location (log scale)")
write_table(core_weed_contrasts, "core_weed_management_contrasts.csv")
write_table(as.data.frame(summary(core_weed_emm)),
            "core_weed_estimated_means.csv")
```

## Core trial: legume biomass (preliminary)

Legume biomass was sampled during peak weed assessment. Of 48 core-trial
observations, many are zero, reflecting both clover termination in tilled
plots and limited persistence in some strip-till plots. The preliminary
additive Tweedie model estimates effects of location, species, and management
on expected legume biomass. It does not test their interactions; interpret
its effects as exploratory, alongside the raw treatment summaries.

```{r core-legume-diagnostics, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
show_diagnostics(core_legume_model)
```

```{r core-legume-anova, results='asis'}
if (!requireNamespace("car", quietly = TRUE)) stop("Install 'car' for Tweedie tests")
if (model_ok(core_legume_model)) {
  core_legume_anova <- as.data.frame(car::Anova(core_legume_model, type = 2))
  core_legume_anova$term <- rownames(core_legume_anova)
  rownames(core_legume_anova) <- NULL
  core_legume_anova <- core_legume_anova[, c("term", setdiff(names(core_legume_anova), "term"))]
  knitr::kable(core_legume_anova, digits = 3,
               caption = "Core legume biomass: preliminary Type II Wald tests")
  write_table(core_legume_anova, "core_legume_anova.csv")
} else {
  cat("Tweedie model inference withheld pending diagnostic review.\n")
}
```

The preliminary model indicates differences by location, clover species,
and management. The management result is expected to be strongly influenced
by the tilled reference, where clover was intentionally terminated. No
post-hoc treatment letters are assigned to this zero-heavy response.

## Musgrave mowing trial: weed biomass (preliminary)

The full split-plot model converges but is singular because the whole-plot
variance is estimated as zero. This is flagged for review rather than silently
removing a random effect or automatically reporting treatment p-values.

```{r mowing-weed-diagnostics, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
show_diagnostics(tool_weed_model)
```

```{r mowing-weed-status}
cat("Singular fit:", lme4::isSingular(tool_weed_model), "\n")
cat("Inferential tests deferred pending random-effects review.\n")
```

## Musgrave mowing trial: legume biomass (preliminary)

All four treatments retain the strip-till system; none deliberately terminate
the entire clover understory. The Tweedie model assesses species and mowing
management additively. Its results should be interpreted cautiously because
yellow sweetclover biomass was near zero in most plots.

```{r mowing-legume-diagnostics, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
show_diagnostics(tool_legume_model)
```

```{r mowing-legume-anova, results='asis'}
if (model_ok(tool_legume_model)) {
  tool_legume_anova <- as.data.frame(car::Anova(tool_legume_model, type = 2))
  tool_legume_anova$term <- rownames(tool_legume_anova)
  rownames(tool_legume_anova) <- NULL
  tool_legume_anova <- tool_legume_anova[, c("term", setdiff(names(tool_legume_anova), "term"))]
  knitr::kable(tool_legume_anova, digits = 3,
               caption = "Musgrave legume biomass: preliminary Type II Wald tests")
  write_table(tool_legume_anova, "musgrave_mowing_legume_anova.csv")
} else {
  cat("Tweedie model inference withheld pending diagnostic review.\n")
}
```

The preliminary model indicates a species effect, with much greater retained
biomass under mammoth red clover, but no detected overall effect of mowing
management. This is not evidence that mowing strategies are equivalent.
The descriptive figure and zero counts remain the clearest summary for now;
we do not perform additional pairwise tests or assign significance letters.

## Interpretation notes

- Core and tool results share Musgrave observations; they are complementary.
- Blocks and whole plots are distinct experimental units, not interchangeable
  subplot replicates.
- In the core trial, legume zeros after Tillage reflect intended clover removal;
  zeros in strip-till treatments may reflect loss of persistence.
- Inspect diagnostics before retaining models, reporting formal conclusions,
  or adding model-based lowercase significance letters to raw-mean figures.
- Wisconsin requires updating design validation and reviewing the model structure.
